steps.text: We map the screens and build rough prototypes — the logic is agreed before any visuals.

faq.answer: A mockup is a picture of particular pages. A design system is the rules and the set of components any page is assembled from, including pages that do not exist yet. It pays for itself around the twentieth screen.

faq.question: What do you work in and what do I get at the end?
faq.answer: We work in Figma. You get a file with prototypes, layouts, a component library and access rights — it stays yours even if a different team takes over later.

faq.question: Can I order design only, without development?
faq.answer: Yes. We hand the layouts and specs to your developers and stay available during the build so the result matches what was designed.

faq.question: How long does it take?
faq.answer: A small site, from two weeks. A service with a client portal and many states, from about six weeks. We name the exact timeline once we have seen how many screens there are.

faq.answer: A logo is only the mark. A visual identity is the system around it: colours, typefaces, collateral and the rules by which they combine. One mark without rules usually falls apart by the third layout.

faq.question: Do we own the rights to the logo?

faq.question: Can it be ordered together with a website?
faq.answer: That is the better order: visual identity first, then the site design built on it. As one project it is both faster and cheaper than doing them separately.

faq.question: What does building a messenger cost?
faq.answer: A first working version with chats, channels and a web interface starts at {price:200000}. A version with files, mobile clients and integrations starts at {price:300000}. A system in a closed network with higher resilience requirements starts at {price:500000}. We refine the estimate once we understand the task: the price depends on the number of users, the storage requirements and which systems the messenger has to talk to.

faq.question: How is this different from a Telegram bot?
faq.answer: A bot lives inside someone else's messenger and solves one specific job: take an enquiry, send a notification. Here you get a product of your own, with your own message database, your own access rights and your own server. If the job is to automate talking to clients in Telegram, you need a bot — that is a separate service.

faq.question: Does the data stay with us?
faq.answer: Yes, that is usually the whole point. The system is deployed on your server or inside a closed network, the message database and the files sit with you, and nothing leaves. We hand over the source code and the documentation, so you are not tied to one contractor afterwards.

faq.question: Can we launch in parts?
faq.answer: That is what we recommend. The first stage is conversations and channels — enough for people to start using it. Files, mobile apps, calls and integrations come after, based on what is actually missing rather than on a list written at the start.

faq.question: What does a website security audit cost?
faq.answer: An express check starts at {price:60000}, a standard audit with manual testing at {price:120000}, and an extended one covering infrastructure and a re-check at {price:240000}. We give an exact figure once we have looked at the site: the price depends on the number of roles, scenarios and external integrations.

faq.question: How is this different from an automated scanner?
faq.answer: A scanner finds known problems: outdated versions, open ports, routine configuration errors. It does not understand your business logic and will not notice that a manager can see someone else's deal by changing an identifier in the URL. Things like that are only found by hand, and they are usually the most expensive ones.

faq.question: Do you only find problems, or can you fix them?
faq.answer: It depends on the plan. Express and Standard end with a report — your developer works from it while we answer questions and later verify that the fixes closed the problem. The Extended plan includes fixing what we found ourselves: we patch the vulnerabilities and re-check the result. That suits teams who have no in-house developer, or none with security experience.

faq.question: Will you break the live site?
faq.answer: No. The testing is non-destructive, and anything potentially risky we agree in advance and run on a copy where possible. Before we start we agree the timing and what to do if something does go wrong.

faq.question: What do we get at the end?
faq.answer: A document a developer can work from: every finding with its severity, a description of how to reproduce it and a recommendation for fixing it. Plus a short summary for management — what is critical, what can be scheduled and what is simply worth knowing.
